_comment: Evisyn criteria for N22 Stroke Prediction (Part II Literature Review). Copied from WritingPapers/evisyn/config/criteria.json template. review_type: RAPID REVIEW (exam deliverable, single reviewer + human gates; not a systematic review).
research_question: Among adults with tabular clinical/EHR risk-factor data, how do machine learning models (ensembles, gradient boosting, stacking) predict stroke compared with logistic regression or classical risk scores, and how do studies handle class imbalance, data splitting/leakage and explainability?

inclusion: Predicts incident stroke risk (or stroke occurrence) from structured tabular data: demographics, comorbidities, vitals, labs or EHR fields
Uses at least one ML model (tree ensemble, boosting, stacking, SVM, neural network) and reports at least one of Recall/Sensitivity, AUC, F1
Peer-reviewed journal article (target SJR Q1/Q2) or double-blind peer-reviewed top conference (MICCAI, MLHC, NeurIPS, IEEE EMBC), published 2020-2026
Systematic reviews of ML for stroke prediction are included as context sources (tagged study_design = Systematic Review)
exclusion: Imaging-only (CT/MRI), signal-only (ECG/EEG) or genomics-only models without tabular risk factors
Post-stroke outcome prediction (mortality, functional outcome, recurrence after a first stroke, hemorrhagic transformation)
Preprints (arXiv/medRxiv) as primary evidence, editorials, letters, conference abstracts without full text
Retracted articles or DOIs that fail Crossref verification
